page: Microsoft Azure E96ds_v6 is an Edsv6-family virtual machine configured with 96 vCPUs and 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations. Storage is provided via 5669 GB of local disk capacity, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core capabilities and exceptional memory throughput. The server achieves top-tier status in uncached large-block memory bandwidth, reaching 506.7 GB/sec for read operations and 207.77 GB/sec for write operations. Multi-threaded performance is further highlighted by strong results in stress-ng multi-core tests and bzip3 decompression. In database and caching benchmarks, the instance demonstrates high efficiency, processing 122.52 million Redis SET operations per second and scoring in the top tier for Passmark database operations. Single-core performance and single-threaded compression tasks fall within the average range.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and substantial local storage, the E96ds_v6 offers high resource density for memory-bound enterprise applications. This hardware profile is highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring large in-memory datasets without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware. It is ideally suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, high-throughput static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing pipelines.
